panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Low-power H&E of patient breast cores showing inflammation centered on ducts and lobules with stromal sparing, the classic lobulocentric pattern of granulomatous lobular mastitis; article title and in-text context confirm IGM. B: H&E at 10x shows periductal granulomatous inflammation with multinucleated giant cells, a characteristic histologic manifestation of idiopathic granulomatous mastitis in a human patient breast core. C: Perilobular inflammation at 10x directly demonstrates granulomatous lobulitis, the defining lobulocentric granulomatous pattern of granulomatous lobular mastitis in patient breast tissue. D: High-power H&E at 40x shows granulomas involving ducts with multinucleated giant cells, the textbook histologic hallmark of idiopathic granulomatous mastitis in a human patient biopsy.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels ((a), (b)). (a): H&E core-biopsy panel at 100x showing an epithelioid granuloma centered on breast lobular acini with lymphocytic infiltrate, matching the lobulocentric non-caseating granuloma of idiopathic granulomatous mastitis; in-text describes neutrophilic microabscesses in the figure. Real human patient histology, disease attribution clear from caption and article title. (b): High-power H&E (400x) view of the same core-biopsy granuloma showing epithelioid histiocytes with lymphocytes and neutrophils, consistent with the epithelioid granuloma and neutrophilic microabscesses described for idiopathic granulomatous lobular mastitis.
